# Forks Tracker & Upstream Merge Policy

> Extracted from CLAUDE.md. Load when auditing forks or evaluating an upstream cherry-pick.

### Upstream Merge Policy — Why We Don't Merge Monstatek

As of April 2026, **we do not merge from Monstatek/M1 upstream**. Reasons:

1. **Upstream is stale.** Monstatek/M1 has been at `v0.8.0.0` since mid-2024 with no
   public commits. There is nothing new to merge.
2. **Divergence is too large.** Hapax has rewritten the build system (CMake + Ninja
   replacing STM32CubeIDE managed makefiles), added 60+ Sub-GHz protocols, a Flipper
   file compatibility layer (`lib/furi/`), CAN bus support, ESP32-C6 SPI AT integration,
   LF-RFID / NFC / IR Flipper import, and a full CI/CD pipeline. A blind merge would
   produce hundreds of conflicts with no benefit.
3. **Version scheme divergence.** Hapax owns `FW_VERSION_MINOR` (9) and `FW_VERSION_RC`.
   Monstatek's version numbering assumptions no longer apply.
4. **Cherry-pick, don't merge.** If Monstatek ever pushes a meaningful update, the
   correct approach is to **review the diff, cherry-pick relevant changes**, and adapt
   them to the Hapax codebase — not to merge the branch wholesale.

If Monstatek publishes a new release in the future, re-evaluate this policy by:
- Fetching `monstatek/main` and inspecting the diff against our `main`
- Cherry-picking any bug fixes or HAL updates that apply
- Bumping `FW_VERSION_MAJOR` only if upstream introduces a breaking API change

a fresh analysis is warranted.  All timestamps are **UTC**.

Rejected/deferred: ESP32 "SPI-slave brain" architecture + ESP-NOW peer link (Hapax owns a divergent, actively-maintained ESP32 integration — see `esp32-coprocessor` skill; a blind port would conflict badly); Sub-GHz "full scene engine" (Hapax already has its own, see `subghz-protocols` skill); portrait/90° orientation mode (large cross-cutting UI rewrite, treat as its own scoped feature if wanted — see `ui-scene-architecture` skill); CDC transmit NULL class-data guard (already present in Hapax `usbd_cdc.c`). **2026-08-09 (session 3)**: Sub-GHz RAW replay full-waveform fix (C3.129/C3.164) cherry-picked — `subghz_replay_flipper_to_tmp()` in `m1_csrc/m1_sub_ghz.c` parsed each `RAW_Data:` line into a hardcoded `uint32_t samples[64]` stack array, so any capture with more than 64 timings per f_gets read silently transmitted only its first 64 samples on replay (e.g. a 512-sample capture sent ~13% of its waveform). Fixed by sizing the parse batch to the full 4096-byte f_gets buffer's capacity via a new shared `SUBGHZ_RAW_LINE_MAX_SAMPLES` (2048) constant in `Sub_Ghz/subghz_raw_line_parser.h`, backed by a static (not stack) `s_raw_sample_batch` array at both RAW_Data call sites; regression test `test_parse_full_line_not_truncated_at_64_samples` added to `tests/test_subghz_raw_line_parser.c` (300-sample line, would have failed truncated at the old 64-sample cap). **2026-08-09 (session 4)**: remainder of the "Device stability hardening" commit `90190c35` cherry-picked (I2C part was already done in session prior review) — (a) USB-MSC `STORAGE_Read`/`STORAGE_Write` in `USB/Class/MSC/Src/usbd_msc_storage.c` had two unconditional `while(1)`/tick-bound spins waiting on the SD-DMA completion queue and card-state transition; both run in USB-ISR context where SysTick can be masked, so a lost/never-posted completion hung the whole USB stack forever while still feeding the IWDG (defeating recovery) — bounded both with a new `MSC_SD_WAIT_MAX_SPINS` iteration cap; (b) added `CDC_TxAbort()` (`USB/Class/CDC/Src/usbd_cdc_if.c/h`, flush EP + clear TxState) and wired it into `vSer2UsbTask`'s (`m1_csrc/m1_usb_cdc_msc.c`) timeout-without-semaphore path, which previously gave the semaphore back while CDC still owned the shared TX buffer by pointer, letting the next iteration reuse/corrupt it mid-flight; (c) `CDC_Receive_FS`'s first stream-buffer drain block (before appending new USB data) pushed bytes into the stream buffer without notifying `vUsb2SerTask` — only the second drain block notified — a lost-wakeup path now fixed by notifying in both; (d) `vUsb2SerTask`'s `ulTaskNotifyTake(pdTRUE, portMAX_DELAY)` could strand the RX endpoint paused forever on a lost flow-control wakeup (inbound RPC dead until USB re-plug); bounded to 100 ms and added a self-heal re-arm when idle and paused; (e) Field Detector ADC `adc_deinit()`/`adc_read_single()` in `m1_csrc/m1_field_detect.c` had bare `while(){}` register-poll spins with no escape (already-present `ADRDY` wait in the same file used a `HAL_GetTick()+100` bound as precedent) — bounded both to a 10 ms tick-based timeout; (f) `boot_recovery_check()`'s two `FLASH_SR_BSY` spins in `m1_csrc/m1_fw_update_bl.c` bounded with the same `0x02000000` iteration cap C3 uses (SystemInit-time, pre-IWDG, so an unbounded stuck-BSY spin had no recovery path); (g) `infrared_encode_timer_cb`/`battery_info_timer`/`prvScreenTimeoutTimerCb` (`m1_infrared.c`, `m1_power_ctl.c`, `uiView.c`) all called `xQueueSend(main_q_hdl, ..., portMAX_DELAY)`/`m1_app_send_q_message()` (which itself blocks on `portMAX_DELAY`) from the shared FreeRTOS timer-service task — a momentarily-full `main_q_hdl` would wedge every software timer in the system (screen timeout included); switched all three to non-blocking (`0` timeout) sends; (h) `m1_wdt_system_check()` in `m1_csrc/m1_watchdog.c` called `M1_LOG_W()`/`m1_wdt_failure_handler()` from inside `taskENTER_CRITICAL()`/`taskEXIT_CRITICAL()` — `M1_LOG_*` takes a mutex+queue, illegal with the scheduler suspended and a risk of hanging/corrupting the watchdog task itself (which then stops feeding the IWDG); the OK/suspended/failure decision is now made via a new pure helper `m1_csrc/m1_watchdog_decision.h` (`m1_wdt_decide_action()`, regression-tested in `tests/test_watchdog_decision.c`) while still inside the critical section, with all logging and the failure handler moved to run after `taskEXIT_CRITICAL()`. Mount-failure card exposure (`SD_access_UnMounted` vs `SD_access_NotOK` in `m1_sdcard_mount()`) reviewed but left as-is pending a closer look at Hapax's already-diverged `SD_access_NotReady`/`NotOK` state machine — tracked as a follow-up, not blindly ported to avoid regressing existing SD recovery behavior. **Recovery FW build variant (`-DRECOVERY=ON`) is DEFERRED per owner prerogative** (2026-08-09) — not a technical blocker, an explicit decision not to pursue it at this time; do not re-propose without the owner raising it. **2026-08-09 (session 7)**: began the next outstanding item, `rpc_task`/SD-detection watchdog supervision + SD self-heal (C3.157). |

### How to Update This Table

1. **When to check**: Before starting any task that involves porting features,
   comparing implementations, or auditing upstream changes.  Also check
   periodically (roughly monthly) or when the user asks.
2. **Discover new forks**: Search GitHub for `M1 in:name fork:true monstatek`
   and for forks of related repos (`bedge117/m1-sdk`,
   `bedge117/esp32-at-monstatek-m1`).  Add any new public fork to the table.
3. **Update existing rows**: For each **Active** fork, fetch the latest commit
   SHA and date.  Compare with the "Latest Commit" column.  If the SHA has
   changed, the fork has new work — update the SHA, date, and bump "Last
   Reviewed by Hapax" to the current UTC timestamp after reviewing.
4. **Classify activity**:
   - **Active** — fork has custom commits beyond stock Monstatek and has been
     updated within the last 60 days.
   - **Inactive** — no custom commits, or last update > 60 days ago.
5. **Record cherry-picks**: When a commit or feature is cherry-picked from a
   fork into Hapax, note it in the "Notes" column (e.g. "C3.4 crash fix
   cherry-picked").
6. **Never remove rows** — mark forks as Inactive instead, so agents know
   the fork was already evaluated.
